reason: Both hit the core points: workflow and system-of-record lock-in, proprietary data, distribution, and the model as a non-moat. A has a good "free tomorrow" test and a sensible ranking. But it dismisses "we're faster", which partly conflicts with iteration speed being the key advantage. B adds decision-changing content: using the 6-month lead to lock in contracts and import data, distilling cheap models and routing only hard cases to the APIs, eval-driven model hot-swapping, and the B2B vs B2C caveat. Its percentages are speculative but not misleading. B is more actionable for the stated situation.
